chapter_title: Concerning the Four Things over which People kill each other.
chapter_note: This chapter is dominated by paraenetic/ethical application (worldly obsessions; exhortation to accept faith), with a formulaic dialogue opening. It lacks the systematic cosmos→cosmos correspondential mappings, degree-structures, or impersonal cosmological mechanics that mark the oldest teaching substrate. The brief Light/Darkness language is embedded inside exhortation and functions as application rhetoric rather than standalone cosmological exposition.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Formulaic dialogue frame (“Once again he speaks to his disciples”), characteristic of the later editorial container.
Ethical/application list item (food/body swelling) with no cosmological mechanism or correspondential mapping; fits institutional paraenesis layer rather than substrate.
Sex/fornication polemic in contemporary moral register; no internal cosmic architecture is being described.
Wealth/riches as moral critique; again application-to-life content without cosmological exposition.
War/tyranny/glory described as social behaviour (‘received a name in the world’), pointing outward to human society rather than mapping within the cosmic system.
Generalizing application voice about ‘all people’ siding with these things; social exhortation register.

Direct address (“I say to you… accept faith”) and soteriological exhortation. The ‘physician… separates the light from the darkness’ phrase appears as applied rhetoric within the exhortation rather than an impersonal cosmological procedure; no clean, self-contained substrate unit is recoverable here.
Moral conclusion about impermanence and death; application register, not systematic cosmology.
